items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I heard, gee, about 1923 with Mamie Smith’s group, you know, I think Mamie Smith and Her Jazz Hounds.

ctx.x: Another musician from that band we really didn’t get into too much was Chu Berry. Do you recall how you became aware of him and hired him for your band?

No. You just became aware of people by being on the scene. You hear them in some setting, or you hear of them and then you hear them. But this much later, I can’t say how or when, you know, I met or heard any of these particular guys, other than Coleman Hawkins, whom I heard, gee, about 1923 with Mamie Smith’s group, you know, I think Mamie Smith and Her Jazz Hounds. But other people, you know, I didn’t hear even much on the jobs at first, you know. Maybe somebody said, “Well, gee, you should hear this guy.” I’d…
Chu Berry’s style when he was with your band, did you . . . I mean, how was he in relation to Coleman Hawkins, to their playing? Was he distinctive at that time?
